question: Should OpenClaw adopt this shared localization runtime and Gateway presentation-metadata contract as a supported cross-surface architecture, or should the work be narrowed to independently owned localization improvements?
rationale: The branch adds a new workspace package, expands a Gateway command contract, and establishes behavior for safety-critical approvals across several owners; correctness alone cannot determine the permanent API and ownership boundary.

options.title: Pause for RFC and owner approval
options.body: Keep the draft open while maintainers decide the localization contract, owner boundaries, and compatibility policy before requesting a narrowed implementation.

options.title: Sponsor the architecture
options.body: Explicitly approve the shared package and Gateway metadata direction, then request owner-scoped compatibility and current-head proof for each adopted surface.

options.title: Narrow to existing surfaces
options.body: Decline the shared contract for now and invite focused PRs that improve already-supported UI or channel translations without new cross-surface APIs.

recommendation.title: Pause for RFC and owner approval
recommendation.body: Keep the draft open while maintainers decide the localization contract, owner boundaries, and compatibility policy before requesting a narrowed implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor is the visible proposer of the RFC-linked foundation series and can provide the design rationale and intended contract scope for maintainer review.
